slides.texte_overlay:
quiet skills that make people
think you're a genius

summarising in one line

after any meeting, video or book, sum it up in one sentence. people who can compress a long idea into a short line always sound like the smartest in the room.

asking the second why

when someone explains something, ask why one more time than feels polite. the second answer is where the real understanding lives, and few people ever get there.

remembering numbers

learn a handful of useful numbers by heart: distances, dates, populations. dropping one accurate figure into a conversation makes everything you say more credible.

knowing a bit of everything

spend 5 minutes a day learning something outside your field: art, history, science. people assume you're a genius when you can talk calmly about almost anything.
slides.texte_sophia:
knowing a bit of everything

i used to only know my own subject. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: art, history, science. people assume you're a genius when you know a bit of everything.

slides.texte_overlay:
saying i'm not sure

admit when you don't know, then say how you'd find out. confident uncertainty sounds far smarter than a guess, and people trust you more because of it.
